purpose: Records the 2026-09-30 fix of the required osv-scanner check, which fails on fresh runs since OSV records five advisories published that day (14:46Z to 15:41Z): GHSA-8988-9cw3-xx77, GHSA-vxq7-64xx-v4gw and GHSA-gh4c-6fx4-qh6g (urllib3 2.7.0, all fixed in 2.8.0) and GHSA-42vr-xj54-vc7v (PyJWT below 2.15.0, fixed in 2.15.0) in the OpenHands recipe lock, and GHSA-vcvr-r3jv-pc5j (next 16.3.5, fixed in 16.3.6) in the frozen macOS variant lock. The OpenHands lock is relocked onto urllib3 2.8.0 and PyJWT 2.15.0 with the recipe's own method (only those two entries change); the macOS lock is a frozen evidence artifact for which the tree records no owner, and it gets a dated ignore under the repository's policy, an IGNORE_ALLOWED_LOCKS row and npm lock readers that bound the repo-wide ignore. One change carries all of it, because the check scans the whole inventory. The name of this record predates the PyJWT advisory, whose fix joined the change once the workspace's 7-day window opened (section B, 16:56:34Z).
authorization: Started from a peer report that the required check failed on fresh runs (peer messages are not retained evidence; the reproduction in section E is). The lock lane is the OpenHands recipe's. For the frozen macOS lock the tree records no owner (returned outputs, section F: its only commit is #201, its experiment record has no owner, session or author key, docs/lanes.md does not name it). No user decision is needed: every fix follows the repository's own policy and method.
evidence_class: Local runs on this host of the pinned OSV-Scanner 2.6.0 with the repository's config and the workflow's command line (reports retained), a local reproduction of the relock with uv 0.12.17 from the pinned upstream source archive, the recipe's own install sequence in a scratch venv, reads of git objects, the OSV API and PyPI, and two 5 read-only cross-family reviews (codex exec as typed in relock-2026-09-30-urllib3.cross-family-review.sh.txt; their own output records no model or effort). Static and local; not an execution of the recipe, of any worker or of any application.
limitations: The relock covers only the recipe venv. The agent-server image's server is a PyInstaller build of upstream's unchanged uv.lock (pins.json source_archive), which still pins urllib3 2.7.0 and PyJWT 2.13.0 or older, and the grader venv has its own lock; neither is changed here (the same scope limit as the earlier PyJWT relock record).

The macOS ignore is a statement about this repository only: it keeps the variant's package.json and lock (two files, no application source), so it says nothing about the application that ran on the Mac on 2026-09-24. It expires on 2026-12-24 and then needs a renewed dated reason, or the lock leaving the inventory.

The next guard (npm_next_pins) follows OSV-Scanner 2.6.0's extractors (osv-scalibr 3090dbb7aaa2, the commit its go.mod pins) for the canonical output of each tool: pnpm-lock.yaml at lockfileVersion 9 (every YAML document; the `packages` entries with their own name and version, as OSV reads them), package-lock.json and npm-shrinkwrap.json (lockfileVersion 1 to 3) and yarn.lock (classic and berry, with npm: aliases). bun.lock, bun.lockb, deno.lock, any other npm format and any style outside the canonical subset have no reader, so such a lock added to the inventory fails the test until one exists (fail closed). It reads pins, not reachability. The yarn and package-lock readers are exercised by unit tests only, because the inventory has no yarn.lock and one package-lock.json without next; the pnpm reader also reads the two real pnpm locks.

Section E of the returned outputs is a local run of the workflow's command on the working tree, not the CI run; the required check on the merged head is the CI result. The failing set is whatever OSV lists at the time of a scan (each scan carries its time), and more advisories can land before a merge.

A separately drafted OpenHands 1.50 Linux lock (draft PR 535, head 00aa6c25fe6f27e9f5974e9f6a5592aa31683479 as fetched, sha256 383ccc5b87702174e471732872f002f1621186710402d048acc2b1910306e106) carries urllib3 2.7.0 and pyjwt 2.14.0 too (section G); this change does not touch its files.

Mutants: the script prints 36 PASS lines (section H): in-memory mutants that must each fail the named guard rule, direct assertions (three of them inputs that must NOT be flagged), and two control runs of the unmutated tests.

The readers decide only the `next` pins of a lock; they do not validate a whole file. A pnpm or yarn file with unparsable lines outside the parts they read is not rejected by them (the scanner's own parse fails on it separately), so `invalid [` lines do not make them return None.
